newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU resolution calls for stronger EMU, jobs link.
newsitem.headline: EU resolution calls for stronger EMU, jobs link.

text.p: The European Union's resolution on growth and employment approved on Monday calls for stronger links between economic and monetary union (EMU) and employment, according to a copy obtained by Reuters.

It also says there should be more coordination between EU countries on jobs policy, moves to create a tax environment conducive to job creation and calls on the European Investment Bank (EIB) to lend to small businesses involved in high-technology.

In addition, the resolution called on EU finance ministers to study future relations between the euro and currencies outside monetary union while preserving the price stability objective of a European Central Bank.

Regarding the links the between EMU and jobs growth, a critical aspect of Monday's agreement, the resolution said: "We will need to strengthen the links between a successful and sustainable Economic and Monetary Union, a well-functioning Internal Market and employment."

The new French government has argued forcefully for greater attention to the plight of Europe's unemployed, and the resolution, while not binding, included language which was seen meeting those demands.
One of the more important aspects of the agreement was to include a greater role for the European Investment Bank, one of the world's largest development agencies.
The Bank was asked to examine "the establishment of a facility for the financing of high-technology projects of small and medium-sized enterprises in cooperation with the European Investment Fund."
Such a facility could possibly make use of venture capital and involve the private banking sector.
While the stability and growth pact remained untouched, the resolution also called for enhanced coordination on jobs policies and tax incentives for employment.
EU leaders stressed "the importance for the member states of creating a tax environment that stimulates enterprise and the creation of jobs," the resolution said.
